title: How This Was Built, Reality Checks & Primary Sources
section: 1. How This Site Was Built (AI + Reproducible Pipeline Disclosure)
text:
1. How This Site Was Built (AI + Reproducible Pipeline Disclosure)
This website and companion PDF brief were scoped, steered, and reviewed by Matthew R.V. Ross (CSU faculty) using Google DeepMind’s Antigravity agentic coding environment to build an end-to-end reproducible R (4.5.2) + Quarto (1.10) pipeline (src/00_setup_theme.R through src/05_verify_audit.R).
Rather than relying on unverified AI summaries or back-of-the-envelope estimates, every chart, metric, and table on this site is computed directly in R from archived primary public files. Equally important, six explicit reality checks were added during construction to catch both AI mistakes and common misconceptions in campus budget debates:

Primary-Source-Only Data Provenance (70 SHA-256 Checksummed Files): Script 01_fetch_sources.R archived 70 public PDFs, HTML governance memos, and federal/BLS API tables across CSU Office of Budgets, CSU IRP&E Fact Books, CDHE Format 30/20 Budget Data Books, CSU System Audited Financial Statements (FY15–FY25), Colorado Office of the State Auditor (OSA) statutory NCAA Agreed-Upon Procedures reports (2516F-B, 2505F-B), BLS CPI-U (CUUR0000SA0), and Urban Institute IPEDS (2015–2023), logging exact URLs, byte counts, and SHA-256 digests in data/sources_manifest.csv.
Visual Slide Inspection (Zero Estimation on Blank Online Exports): Automated PDF text extraction missed embedded images in 2026 campus budget forum decks, so every slide was rasterized and inspected visually. That check caught that Slides 14–15 of the posted Oct. 14, 2026 PDF contained blank white table placeholders online—so the pipeline drew the $61.3M–$70.7M shortfall and ~$25.0M enrollment drop exclusively from the Oct. 7, 2026 campus memo and May 13 V4 Slide 6 ($15.112M expiring one-time stopgaps) instead of guessing missing numbers.
Domain Reality Check on Soft-Money Research Staff (CEMML / CIRA / VTH): Early exploratory drafts risked treating CSU’s campus-wide staff growth (~3:1 ratio) as uniform “administrative overhead.” Human domain review explicitly required separating self-funding sponsored research and enterprise units (Table 123 and Table 124), establishing that 69.7% (3,205.5 of 4,597.7) of FY25 Administrative Professional FTE sit outside E&G—including 96.3% non-E&G in WCNR (home to CEMML) and 82.1% non-E&G in Engineering (CIRA).
Controls for Cross-Year Accounting Shifts: CSU’s Office of Budgets ColOBS files reflect two major structural accounting reclassifications: moving $41.64M of financial aid from XA Central into P1 Enrollment & Access in FY19, and decentralizing ~$111.26M of pooled XA Employee Fringe Benefits into individual divisions in FY26. Both shifts are documented and controlled in Figure 5 so accounting transfers are not misread as sudden administrative spending surges.
Two-Way Claim Verification & Non-Interpolation: Circulating claims from multiple perspectives were audited symmetrically against public filings—verifying Parsons’ $1.1M settlement/non-disparagement terms, Coach Jim Mora Jr.’s $2.4M base contract, Athletics’ $75.24M gross vs. ~$15.57M net operating support, and $206.96M Athletics debt; documenting that public San Francisco Chronicle reporting on Title IX investigator Jeffrey Lamoureaux involved universities outside CSU; and leaving omitted FY21–FY24 E&G State Classified rows in Fact Book Table 128 as NA rather than interpolating.
Automated Reconciliation Suite (src/05_verify_audit.R) & Visual Layout Checks: Seven automated assertions verify ledger balances ($54.272M V4 closeout sums to $0; $61.3M–$70.7M FY28 steps sum cleanly; FY27 unit cuts equal 160.58 FTE; Table 124 AP FTE reconciles to 1,392.2 E&G / 3,205.5 non-E&G; OSA revenues/expenses/debt tie out), followed by automated HTML DOM checks (zero accidental math mode, zero broken links) and visual inspection of rendered figures and PDF tables.

If any member of the CSU community—faculty, staff, administration, or board—spots an accounting nuance, classification correction, or missing primary record, please open an issue or pull request on github.com/matthewross07/csu_budget_context.

2. Accounting Scope & Deflation Notes

CSU System vs. Fort Collins Standalone Scope (finstmt2015–2025 vs. BDB/ColOBS/OSA):

CSU System Audited Statements combine Fort Collins, CSU Pueblo, and System/SPUR ($644.9M net tuition, 21.3% discount rate, $1,330.7M long-term debt in FY25 + $79.1M STRATA ATLAS Laser bonds issued June 26, 2025).
Fort Collins Standalone Scope comes from CDHE Format 30/20 Budget Data Books (FINAL_BDB), CSU Office of Budgets Operating Budget Summaries (ColOBS + OBS), IRP&E Fact Books (Tables 122–128), and Note 5 of Colorado OSA Report 2516F-B ($1,118.77M Fort Collins total debt, including $206.96M Athletics debt).

Real-Dollar Deflation (CPI-U, macro_cpiu_fy.csv):

Monthly BLS CPI-U All Urban Consumers (CUUR0000SA0, 2014–Oct 2026) is averaged across CSU’s July–June fiscal calendar so multi-year net tuition and debt series are evaluated in constant FY25 or FY26 purchasing power (FY27 covers Jul–Oct 2026).

title: Athletics Accounting & Long-Term Capital Debt Context
text: Placing a $75.24M gross Athletics budget alongside a $61.3M–$70.7M E&G operating gap makes it natural to ask whether restructuring or reducing Athletics could close the university’s shortfall. Audited filings from the Colorado Office of the State Auditor (csu_ncaa_aup_fy19.pdf–fy25.pdf, Report 2516F-B) clarify both sides of that question: Athletics represents a real ongoing subsidy (~15–20% of Ledger B’s multi-year structural pressures), yet gross expenditure numbers substantially overstate how much general-fund cash could be freed quickly.

title: Understanding CSU’s FY27–28 Operating Budget Gap
text:
Purpose & Shared Context: Colorado State University (Fort Collins) enters late 2026 governance discussions—including the Nov. 30 AAUP chapter meeting, Dec. 1 Faculty Council, and Dec. 3–4 Board of Governors meetings—facing a projected $61.3M–$70.7M FY28 Education & General (E&G) budget gap. Recent leadership transitions, including Former President Amy Parsons’ $1.1M transition settlement/non-disparagement agreement and high-profile athletics contracts, have raised fair questions about governance, priorities, and communication. At the same time, primary public financial records show that the FY28 shortfall reflects deeper multi-year trends—non-resident enrollment shifts, expiring one-time stopgaps, state funding constraints, permanent E&G payroll commitments across both administrative and academic units, and capital debt service—that affect CSU regardless of individual personnel decisions.
To make productive campus dialogue easier, this resource separates short-run FY28 budget mechanics (Ledger A) from multi-year structural pressures (Ledger B) using 70 archived public documents logged in data/sources_manifest.csv. Rather than assigning blame to any single constituency, the goal is to ensure faculty, staff, deans, VPs, and board members are working from the same audited numbers.

How This Site Was Built & Reality Checks Applied

Transparency & Build Disclosure: This site was initiated and reviewed by Matthew R.V. Ross (CSU faculty) using Google DeepMind’s Antigravity agentic coding environment to assemble a fully reproducible R (4.5.2) + Quarto (1.10) pipeline (src/00–src/05). Because automated tools and public commentary can both make mistakes, six explicit reality checks were built into the workflow:

Primary-Source-Only Ingestion: Every chart and table is computed programmatically from 70 downloaded primary PDFs and public federal APIs archived with SHA-256 hashes in data/sources_manifest.csv.
Visual Inspection of Posted Slides (Zero Guessing): Rasterized slide decks revealed that Slides 14–15 of the posted Oct. 14, 2026 PDF had blank scenario table placeholders online; rather than estimating values, Ledger A relies strictly on the Oct. 7, 2026 memo and May 13 V4 Slide 6.
Soft-Money Research Distinction (CEMML / CIRA / VTH): Human domain review explicitly required splitting non-E&G research/enterprise AP roles (69.7% campus-wide; 96.3% in WCNR/CEMML) from general-fund E&G lines (Table 124) so self-funding grant staff are not lumped into structural E&G overhead.
Accounting Reclassification Controls: Historical ColOBS series isolate both FY19’s $41.64M financial-aid shift (XA to P1) and FY26’s ~$111.26M fringe decentralization so accounting moves are not mistaken for sudden spending spikes.
Two-Way Claim Verification & Non-Interpolation: Both leadership statements and circulating faculty claims were cross-checked against public records—flagging, for instance, that public San Francisco Chronicle reporting on Title IX investigator Jeffrey Lamoureaux involved other universities rather than CSU, and leaving omitted FY21–FY24 E&G State Classified rows in Fact Book Table 128 as NA without interpolation.
Automated Reconciliation Checks (src/05_verify_audit.R): Seven programmatic verification checks validate all sums, splits, and outputs on every run. Full methodology and data limitations appear on How This Was Built.

Ledger A Overview: Immediate Drivers of CSU’s Projected $61.3M–$70.7M FY28 Operating Gap




Ledger A: FY28 Gap reviews the $61.3M–$70.7M projection alongside Fall 2026 census shifts (-2.5% RI enrollment, -9.7% Domestic Non-Resident UG, 4-year graduation rising to 55.1%) and FY27 V4 closeout figures ($15.112M expiring one-time savings and 160.58 permanent FTE reductions across colleges and support units).
Ledger B: Structural Context disaggregates E&G personnel from externally funded research staff like WCNR/CEMML (96.3% non-E&G), examines 10-year E&G growth across both admin (+62.3%) and faculty (+43.3%, primarily CCA/NTT), and reviews tuition discounting (21.3%) and Colorado funding constraints.
Athletics & Debt reconciles the $75.24M gross Athletics budget down to ~$15.57M net operating support, details CSU’s $206.96M Athletics bonded debt (18.5% of campus debt), and evaluates football cancellation and NCAA tournament scenarios objectively.
Governance & Peers examines trust-related governance questions, documents a factual source check on Title IX hiring claims, benchmarks CSU against 7 Colorado and land-grant R1 peers (IPEDS FY23), and outlines constructive questions ahead of the FY28 Hybrid RCM transition.
How This Was Built documents the full build pipeline, AI/human verification safeguards, accounting scope notes, upstream portal blocks (DATA_GAPS.md), and all 70 primary sources.


Downloadable Brief: A formatted 12-page PDF Brief (Understanding CSU’s FY27–28 Operating Budget Gap) is also available for committee packets or offline reading.

2. State Funding Limits, Tuition Discounting & Research F&A Mechanics




Accounting-Adjusted E&G Division Trends (FY15–FY26), Institutional Discounting Rate, and Non-Resident Share



Three structural revenue constraints help explain why strong campus activity—like rising grant totals and full teaching loads—does not automatically eliminate an E&G operating gap:

Higher Institutional Tuition Discounting: In CSU System audited financial statements (audits_system_fy15_fy25), scholarship allowances increased from $114.4M (19.9% discount rate in FY15; 17.9% in FY17) to $174.1M (21.3% discount rate) in FY25. Within Fort Collins E&G budgets (bdb_real_fy17_fy27), institutional aid grew from $47.2M (FY15) to $88.5M (FY26) and $96.3M estimated for FY27, offsetting part of headline tuition rate increases (3.5% resident / 4.0% NR / 3.5% differential in FY27).
State Funding Constraints: In FY27 (obs_state_approp_fy24_fy27), State Fee-for-Service ($161.60M) and COF stipends ($49.45M) supply $211.05M (23.4% of the $900.98M State Appropriated / E&G budget)—virtually flat versus FY26 ($210.94M) under Colorado’s TABOR limits and state Medicaid pressures.
Why Sponsored Research Grants Do Not Directly Cross-Subsidize E&G Instruction: CSU System grants and contracts reached $548.0M in FY25 (audits) and Fort Collins Indirect Cost Recovery (IDCR) reached $76.0M (obs). However, federal F&A recovery partially reimburses dedicated research compliance, startup packages, cost-share commitments, and lab infrastructure rather than generating surplus cash for general undergraduate instruction. Similarly, higher teaching loads in discounted resident programs add instructional workload with lower net margin than non-resident enrollment.

text: Addressing a multi-year budget adjustment constructively requires two forms of honesty at once: recognizing where leadership decisions genuinely strained campus trust, and checking circulating claims carefully against primary public records.

title: Trust, Source Verification & Peer Benchmarks
section: 1. Governance & Trust Concerns vs. Source Verification
text:
1. Governance & Trust Concerns vs. Source Verification

Documented Leadership & Communication Concerns

Former President Amy Parsons’ Resignation & $1.1M Transition Settlement (Oct. 28 – Nov. 5, 2026): On Oct. 28, 2026, CSU announced Parsons’ resignation effective Dec. 31, 2026 (prior contract ran to Jan. 2028 at $600k/yr; Rick Miranda serves as Interim President beginning Jan. 1, 2027), alongside a $1.1M transition payout and mutual non-disparagement clause criticized by AAUP-CSU on Nov. 5 (aaupcsu.org). While $1.1M one-time equals 1.7% of one year’s $66.0M FY28 operating projection, non-disclosure terms around executive departures understandably weaken confidence when units across campus have just absorbed 160.58 permanent FTE reductions.
Football Coaching Contract & Public Optics ($2.4M Base): Head Football Coach Jim Mora Jr.’s 5-year contract (opening at $2.4M base pay and escalating to $2.8M), alongside post-game remarks following a 73–7 loss at Washington State (“These are people here that don’t know how to win”), drew sharp campus criticism during an E&G hiring slowdown—though reducing that salary alone would resolve <4% of Ledger A.



Source Verification Note: Title IX Investigator Jeffrey Lamoureaux

Fact-Check Note Ahead of Late-2026 Meetings: Recent campus commentary has cited the hiring of Title IX investigator Jeffrey Lamoureaux, pointing to prior San Francisco Chronicle reporting as evidence of vetting lapses at CSU. Primary records audited for this project do not show an employment link between Jeffrey Lamoureaux and CSU Fort Collins.

What San Francisco Chronicle / UC Berkeley IRP actually reported: Former Burbank Police Sgt. Jeffrey Lamoureaux left law enforcement under a California “clean-record agreement” and later worked as a Title IX investigator at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL), Eastern Washington University, Appalachian State, Goodwin University, Auburn University, and the University of San Francisco. Colorado appeared in that reporting because state legislators enacted statutory restrictions on similar police clean-record agreements—not due to CSU employment.
Why accuracy helps campus dialogue: Relying strictly on verified Colorado public records—such as the $1.1M non-disparagement payout, capital debt trajectories ($1.33B System debt), and FY22–FY25 E&G hiring patterns (Table 128)—keeps discussions focused on verifiable institutional facts rather than disputable personnel claims.

text:
3. Constructive Questions Ahead of the FY28 Hybrid RCM Transition
In their Oct. 26, 2026 memo (alongside Faculty Fellows Rob Mitchell and Jennifer Martin), campus leadership noted transparently: “Changing the budget model will not by itself close a budget shortfall, nor does it produce new funding.” With FY27 serving as the Parallel Year ahead of July 1, 2027 implementation, shared governance, deans, and administration have practical opportunities to focus on the right ledgers:

Clarify Post-FY22 E&G Central VP Hiring (864.8 FTE = 62.1% of E&G AP): Review which portions of the +326 E&G Admin Pro positions added between FY22 and FY25 sit in central administrative offices versus student-success, compliance, or college operations—explicitly separating grant-funded WCNR/CEMML and Engineering/CIRA roles.
Co-Design Transparent FY28 Hybrid RCM Rules: Publish clear parameters ahead of Dec. 3–4 BOG review covering “off-the-top” central assessments (XA Debt Service $31.86M, CSU Spur $15.00M), instructional credit-hour weights, and subvention mechanisms for foundational disciplines.
Align Long-Term Athletics & Debt Planning With E&G Capacity: Evaluate multi-year glide paths for CSU’s ~$15.6M net Athletics operating support (B2 $17.15M FY26 base) alongside cautious policies on any new bonded or internal treasury debt while general funds remain tight.
Track Net Tuition Yield Alongside Enrollment Headcounts: As campus recruits both resident and non-resident cohorts (-9.7% Dom NR UG in Fall 2026), measure net revenue per seat net of institutional discounting ($174.1M System allowance / 21.3% discount rate) so enrollment strategies strengthen net margins.
